public_rationale: There is credible evidence of regressions on particular tasks and in preferences between particular versions. There is also evidence of improvements. Neither establishes the overall rate of progress across LLM services. The regression component has support, but the broader slowdown claim remains unsettled; improvements alone would not refute slower improvement.
limitations: The comparison window and scope are not specified by Zitron.
Task scores, formatting compliance and user preferences measure different things.
This assessment concerns the period before the post, not subsequent AI progress.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Improvement in LLM-based services like ChatGPT has slowed and even regressed.

statement.excerpt: In many respects, this comparison is eerily prophetic, given the slowdown (and even regression) of improvement we’ve seen in LLM-based services like ChatGPT.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that useful capabilities were improving more slowly, with some capabilities getting worse.
I use 2023 through the post date as the comparison window for successive service versions. The speaker supplies neither a starting date nor a reporting period; this window is an evaluator choice.
A slowdown requires comparisons of gains across successive intervals. A decline on one task establishes a local regression, but does not by itself establish a general slowdown.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable longitudinal evaluations show diminishing gains across a representative set of capabilities, together with reproducible regressions on some tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable longitudinal evaluations show sustained or accelerating gains across representative capabilities and fail to substantiate the alleged regressions. Improvements on selected tasks alone do not disprove a slowdown.

evidence.publisher: arXiv; Lingjiao Chen, Matei Zaharia and James Zou
evidence.explanation: This supports the regression component for particular service behaviors. The same abstract reports improvements on other tasks, so it does not establish a general decline or a slowing rate of improvement.

evidence.locator: Tracking Performance of Proprietary APIs - GPT-4-0314 vs 0613?
evidence.explanation: Users preferred the earlier GPT-4 version, supporting a local service regression. The authors also identify changing users and comparison sets as possible explanations; their table places GPT-4 Turbo above the June version.

evidence.locator: Full Leaderboard with GPT-4-Turbo as judge, explanatory paragraph and following table
evidence.explanation: The table scores April GPT-4 Turbo at 82.6 against 50.0 for the March 2023 baseline, showing improvement on this evaluation. The authors warn about model-judge bias; these comparisons do not measure whether progress was slowing.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative evaluation of successive service versions across multiple intervals, using stable tasks and scoring, that establishes whether capability gains were diminishing.
